title: Strengthening Singapore’s Position as a Global Hub for Talent
what_it_is: Strengthening Singapore’s Position as a Global Hub for Talent

sections.label: New pass and EP changes
sections.summary: Introduces the ONE Pass and new benchmarks, restores FCF advertising to 14 days, and offers five-year EPs for tech occupations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: First, a new Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass (ONE Pass) for talent earning at least $30,000 in fixed monthly salary, comparable to the top 5% of Employment Pass (EP) holders or with outstanding achievements in arts and culture, sports and research and academia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Second, a new benchmark pegged to the top 10% of EP holders for our existing schemes, namely, the exemption from the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) job advertising requirement and Complementarity Assessment framework (COMPASS) as well as salary criterion for the Personalised Employment Pass (PEP).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Third, restoring the FCF job advertising duration from 28 days to 14 days with effect from 1 September 2022 and improving the processing time of EP applications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Lastly, the option of a five-year EP to experienced professionals filling tech occupations on the COMPASS Shortage Occupation List (SOL).

sections.label: ONE Pass versus Tech.Pass
sections.summary: The ONE Pass is open to all sectors, not just tech, and lasts five years instead of two.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: But compared to the Tech.Pass, it is open to candidates from all sectors and is not limited to the tech sector alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It has a longer duration of five years instead of two years.

sections.label: ONE Pass criteria questions
sections.summary: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman and Mr Pritam Singh asked for more details on criteria for talent with outstanding achievements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Turning to the criteria for the ONE Pass, Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman and Mr Pritam Singh have asked for more details on the criteria for talent with outstanding achievements who do not need to meet the salary criterion of $30,000.

sections.label: Salary and employer criteria
sections.summary: The $30,000 fixed monthly salary must come from one employer, and overseas employers must meet market capitalisation or revenue thresholds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In general, the fixed monthly salary of $30,000 must be from one employer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For overseas candidates, the previous or prospective employer must also have a market capitalisation of at least US$500 million or an annual revenue of at least US$200 million.

sections.label: No quota for ONE Pass
sections.summary: 5% of EP holders is around 8,000, and no quota will be set on ONE Pass holders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To give a sense of numbers, 5% of our EP holders today would be around 8,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman, Mr Pritam Singh and Ms He Ting Ru have also asked whether we will be setting a quota on the number of ONE Pass holders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are not setting a quota and the reason is this – if we accept that there is never enough of top talent to go around the world, then it does not make sense for us to limit the amount of talent we are bringing in.

sections.label: No quota given higher bar
sections.summary: Because the ONE Pass has a higher quality bar than an EP, applying a quota would not be wise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Given that the ONE Pass has an even higher quality bar than an EP, it would not be wise for us to apply a quota here.

sections.label: EP exemption threshold increase
sections.summary: Setting the benchmark at the top 10% of EP holders raises the exemption threshold from $20,000 to $22,500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: By setting the benchmark at the top 10% of EP holders, the threshold for exemption is in fact increased from $20,000 to $22,500.

sections.label: Top 10% EP holders
sections.summary: The top 10% of EP holders consists mostly of senior management and senior professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The top 10% of EP holders consists mostly of senior management and senior professionals.

sections.label: Exemption not major concession
sections.summary: Providing this exemption is therefore not a major concession on our part.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Providing this exemption is therefore not a major concession on our part.

sections.label: FCF job advertising duration adjustment
sections.summary: The adjustment to the FCF job advertising duration applies to all EP and S Pass applications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: On that note, let me touch on to the adjustment to the FCF job advertising duration, which applies to all EP and S Pass applications.

sections.label: FCF advertising introduced 2014
sections.summary: When the FCF job advertising requirement was first introduced in 2014, the duration was set at 14 days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: When the FCF job advertising requirement was first introduced in 2014, the duration was set at 14 days.

sections.label: FCF duration extended during COVID-19
sections.summary: During COVID-19, the FCF job advertising duration was extended to 28 days because of unprecedented labour market slack.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: During COVID-19, we extended the FCF job advertising duration to 28 days because of the unprecedented slack in the labour market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The ratio of job vacancies to unemployed persons reached a low of 0.55 in June 2020 in the thick of COVID-19 – there were more jobseekers than job openings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The ratio of vacancies to unemployed persons has risen in excess of 2.4.

sections.label: Job advertisement period adjustment
sections.summary: Companies say the 28-day job advertisement requirement makes them lose candidates, so the period should return to 14 days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Companies, including local enterprises, have been giving feedback that in the tight labour market, the 28-day requirement is causing them to lose good candidates because they are unable to offer them employment contracts quickly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It is timely to adjust the job advertisement period back to 14 days.

sections.label: NTUC Company Training Committee Grant
sections.summary: At Budget this year, the Minister for Finance announced $70 million set aside for the NTUC Company Training Committee Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: At Budget this year, the Minister for Finance also announced that $70 million has been set aside for the NTUC Company Training Committee (CTC) Grant.

sections.label: Skills transfer and ONE Pass
sections.summary: No mandatory skills transfer requirement will be set; MOM announced the Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass for talent earning at least $30,000 monthly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: At the end of the day, skills transfer is not a simple or linear process – it would be impossible to come up with a single rule on how long it should take for skills to be transferred from one person to another, or how much skills to transfer, for that matter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: So, our approach is not to set a mandatory requirement for skills transfer, but rather, to put in place the right ecosystem of policies that incentivises businesses to select complementary foreign workers, while building up a strong Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Last month, MOM announced several targeted enhancements to our work pass framework, including the introduction of a new pass - the Overseas Networks & Expertise (ONE) Pass – in January 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The ONE Pass is meant to attract top talent from all sectors, to strengthen our position as a global hub for talent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It is for talent earning at least $30,000 in fixed monthly salary, comparable to the top 5% of EP holders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The validity period is five years, longer than that of other work passes.

sections.label: Singapore GDP growth
sections.summary: At the start of the 1970s GDP was $20 billion, and the economy has now grown to $454 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: At the start of the 1970s, our GDP was $20 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The opportunities for Singaporeans then were much more limited, in terms of the sectors and occupations that they could work in.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: I mentioned before that our economy has now grown to $454 billion.

sections.label: Work pass framework enhancements
sections.summary: The enhancements to the work pass framework are described as offensives on global talent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The enhancements to our work pass framework are our offensives on global talent.

sections.label: Engaging global talent
sections.summary: Sector agencies are identifying high quality individuals and using networks like EDB's overseas offices to reach global talent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our sector agencies are identifying high quality individuals to proactively engage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will be leveraging existing networks, such as EDB's overseas offices, to reach out to the right global talent.

sections.label: ONE Pass talent quality
sections.summary: The ONE Pass has no fixed number; COMPASS will manage nationality diversity, and it targets the top 5% of EP holders for talent quality.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the ONE Pass, we do not have a fixed number.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The nationality diversity, the nationality concentration, we have envisaged that on a broader perspective, our COMPASS framework will manage that complementarity part.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Because the ONE Pass is really targeted at the top 5% of EP holders, what we are concerned about is really the quality of that talent coming in.

sections.label: Family offices frameworks
sections.summary: Frameworks are being developed for family offices to raise competency and skillsets and groom local talent, including in the green economy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: On family offices, we are developing frameworks in specialised areas in which we are looking at, to up the ante in terms of bringing up the level of competency, the expertise and the skillsets and grooming our local talent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, the family offices, depending on the space that they are in, if they are in the green economy and they are hiring members with that level of expertise and talent to help us to develop sustainable green practices, or in the sustainability space, it is something that we would be prepared to consider.

sections.label: Unpublished ONE Pass criteria
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to confirm whether there are other unpublished eligibility criteria for the ONE Pass.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm if there are any other eligibility criteria for the ONE Pass that have not been published thus far?

sections.label: SkillsFuture subsidies support
sections.summary: The Government has given significant SkillsFuture subsidies, including ESG's Enterprise Development Programme and sector-specific programmes supporting local skillsets.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Government has given significant SkillsFuture subsidies – Enterprise Singapore (ESG)'s Enterprise Development Programme as well as sector-specific programmes where various sector agencies are continually supporting the development of skillsets for our locals.

sections.label: Scheme benefits since 2017
sections.summary: Since its inception in 2017, the scheme has benefited more than 140 companies and more than 1,000 locals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The scheme was created and since its inception in 2017, it has benefited more than 140 companies and more than 1,000 locals.

sections.label: Global talent criteria framework
sections.summary: Work continues with sector agencies, MOE, MCCY and NRF on criteria for global talent, with the scheme starting 1 January 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are working on all the other routes, through different sector agencies, in terms of coming up with a framework and we will also worked, as I have shared, with MOE, with MCCY, with NRF and a few other agencies, to identify some of these criteria in which we can target these global talents with this kind of expertise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, towards the end of the year – the scheme will start on 1 January 2023 – I suggest that he watches this space.

sections.label: ONE Pass holder other companies
sections.summary: The $30,000 comes primarily from one company, but the ONE Pass holder is not restricted from working with other companies to transfer skillsets and expertise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I think his first supplementary question, I have already answered that, primarily, it comes from one company – that $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But we will not restrict the ONE Pass holder from working with other companies if he is able to transfer skillsets and his expertise.

sections.label: FCF job advertisement period reduction
sections.summary: The question asks whether reducing the FCF job advertisement period from 28 to 14 days for EP applications reduces employers' impetus to hire local PMETs, especially mature ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister whether the reductions in the job advertisement period under FCF from 28 days to 14 days for EP applications reduces the impetus for employers to hire local PMETs, especially those in the more mature age groups?

sections.label: Figure as of end-March 2022
sections.summary: As of end-March 2022, the figure was about 2.4.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As of end-March 2022, it was about 2.4.

sections.label: Shortening FCF gives companies breathing space
sections.summary: Shortening the FCF gives companies breathing space to get needed employees to fulfil orders and gear up for new orders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The shortening of the FCF allows some form of a breathing space for our companies to get the employees that they need to help them to fulfil their orders, to help them to also gear up for new orders coming in.

sections.label: ONE Pass benchmark and Singaporeans
sections.summary: With the top 5% EP holder benchmark and $30,000 salary requirement, of about 8,000 foreign EP holders earning at least $30,000, the vast majority of top corporate executives earning $30,000 or more monthly are Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If it is any comfort, when we set the benchmark at the top 5% of EP holders and the $30,000 salary requirement, and we looked at the statistics of the numbers of about 8,000 foreign EP holders who are earning at least $30,000, when we compare to our local Singapore Core, our local Singapore talent, in terms of the numbers, if you look at the entire universe of top corporate executives earning $30,000 or more a month, the Member would be happy to know that the vast majority of them are Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The fundamental objective in creating this ONE Pass is to, if I may use this cliché statement, find new cheese.

sections.label: ONE Pass multiple jobs business
sections.summary: The ONE Pass allows the holder to hold multiple jobs and even start his or her own business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The ONE Pass allows this holder to hold multiple jobs and even starts his or her own business.

sections.label: Sector-specific manpower schemes
sections.summary: The passage states there are sector-specific measures and multiple schemes, including M-SEP, NTSOL, and improvements to S Pass, EP and Work Permit.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the different sectors that he was talking about, it is also important to understand that we have sector-specific measures as well to cater and there are multiple schemes available including in MTI, there is a Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities (M-SEP) to address the much needed workforce gaps in the different sectors including healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We should not look at the ONE Pass in isolation, we should look at the entire improvement in terms of the S Pass, our normal EP as well as the Work Permit.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And including – at my announcement earlier on at COS this year – the introduction of Non-Traditional Sources Occupation List (NTSOL) where companies can hire from non-traditional sources for our Indian restaurants, in terms of Indian chefs.

sections.label: LOC for pass holder spouse
sections.summary: The passage states the LOC is given only to the spouse of the Pass holder, not dependants, and numbers are not envisaged to be high.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: On the LOC given, it is only given to the spouse of the Pass holder.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It is not given to the dependants of the Pass holder.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And like I said, because of the highly selective nature of the scheme, we do not envisage that the numbers will be high, the delta will be high.

sections.label: FCF advertisement response timing
sections.summary: The passage states about 70% of responses to the FCF advertisement happen within the first two weeks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Earlier on, I have shared that about 70% of the responses to the FCF advertisement happens within the first two weeks.

sections.label: COMPASS and Workplace Fairness progress
sections.summary: The passage states the figure has gone up almost fivefold to in excess of 2.4 as of end of March, and policies including COMPASS are on track.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, it has gone up almost fivefold, it is 2.4 as of end of March, now it is in excess of 2.4.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: All of our policies, including the COMPASS framework, we are on track with regard to the Workplace Fairness legislation.

sections.label: Regular evaluation of ONE Pass holders
sections.summary: The passage states sector agencies will work closely to evaluate ONE Pass holders regularly, given the wide diaspora of talent across sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Having said that, because it is a wide diaspora of talent that we are looking at and in different sectors, we will work very closely with the sector agencies to evaluate ONE Pass holders on a very regular basis.

sections.label: Schemes to groom Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage states there are schemes to groom Singaporeans, including MAS iPost, TeSA, Global Ready Talent Programme, and the Singapore Global Executive Programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Simultaneously, in fact, contemporaneously, we have a whole slew of schemes today that we constantly groom and provide that opportunity for our Singaporeans to make sure that they keep abreast and, in some instance, we try to even nudge them to go ahead, think out-of-the box so that they can compete.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have under MAS, we have the International Postings (iPost) Programme which is running very well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: There is the TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) Programme for which we train our tech talent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I have earlier on also shared that we have the Global Ready Talent Programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In March this year, during the Budget and Committee of Supply (COS), we also announced the Singapore Global Executive Programme.

sections.label: Talent competition and Golden Visa
sections.summary: Singapore is not competing with a target country; the UAE Golden Visa reflects different aspirations and constraints, and Singapore starts from strength.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Is this sufficient for us to get our fair share of talent and help companies to grow?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We do not have a target country that we are competing with.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Golden Visa, I presume Mr Desmond Choo is referring to, pertains to UAE.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Their aspirations and our aspirations are actually quite different because of the fact that they have different levels of constraints just like we have our own constraints.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are starting from the position of strength.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We look at potential new enterprises that we see ourselves getting our first mover and our competitive advantage in.
